narrative.overview:
The site is the VoxDSTAR app's own night display, unchanged and enlarged to a browser: a near-black glass ground, a panel-coloured status line on top, a softkey bar along the bottom, hairline dividers between rows, and the reflector shown as a huge mono readout. The page is a memory bank of channels (M01 to M07), and the visitor steps them the way the radio's knob steps memories. Every colour, face and silhouette comes from the app's palette (`RadioViews.kt`, night values) and its screens on the HYT-P50, so an operator who uses the app recognises the page before reading it.

Density is a radio's: words are short, values sit right-aligned in mono, rows are numbered. The palette is dark neutrals with signal colours that each mean one thing: cyan is the link, orange the module and the one action, green receive, red transmit. Nothing is decorative. Depth is a flat set of bands and hairlines, never shadow. Motion is one thing: a channel's readout re-renders in 120ms when it arrives.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, flat display surfaces in the app's exact night colours; no gradients, no shadows.
Three type roles: Barlow for sentences, Barlow Condensed for headings, labels and keys, Share Tech Mono for anything the radio would display (reflector, module, callsign, value, counter).
A sticky status bar and softkey bar frame the page like the app's top and bottom lines.
Signal colours are semantic, each confined to one job.
Radius only on controls and tags; every surface is square.
Real screen captures, shown only at whole-pixel scale.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Each signal colour has one job. Cyan is the link (the reflector chip) and focus; orange is the module letter and the single action; green is receive; red is transmit; amber is the brand mark. A colour never borrows another's job, and none of them fills a resting surface outside its job.

rules.name: The App Palette Rule
rules.body: Neutrals and signal colours are the app's night values (`RadioViews.kt`). Add a colour only if the app has it; never retune one for the web.

rules.name: The Display Data Rule
rules.body: Anything the radio would show as data (reflector, module, callsign, timing, key name, counter) is set in Share Tech Mono; sentences never are.

rules.name: The Uppercase Belongs To Keys Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is for keys, bar labels and mono data the app shows in caps; headings and sentences stay in sentence case.

rules.name: The Memory Bank Rule
rules.body: A page in this system is a sequence of channels stepped by scroll, arrow keys or the strip; new content becomes a channel with its own memory (reflector and module), not a free-standing band.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px hairlines in `line`, never with shadow or tint washes.

dos: **Do** take every colour from the app's night palette and keep each signal colour to its one job (cyan link and focus, orange module and action, green RX, red TX, amber mark).
**Do** set reflectors, modules, callsigns, values and counters in Share Tech Mono, with the module letter in orange.
**Do** mark the active row with the ink selection bar and glass-black text, as the app's menus do.
**Do** show screen captures only at whole-pixel scale (2x on desktop, 1x under 560px) with `image-rendering: pixelated`.
**Do** keep the motion to the 120ms readout re-render, off under reduced motion, and keep the page working as plain anchors without JavaScript.
**Do** draw structure with 1px hairlines and tonal bands.
donts: **Don't** wash the active channel or any resting surface in cyan; cyan at rest is the reflector chip only.
**Don't** use orange for a second action or for decoration; there is one action.
**Don't** use green or red outside the receive and transmit call panels.
**Don't** use brand amber outside the mark and the wordmark's D.
**Don't** add shadows, gradients, or radius on surfaces, panels or frames.
**Don't** scale captures to fractional sizes or let them smooth.
**Don't** add slides, smooth scrolling or easing to channel changes.
